title: Wearable Sensors for Assessing Risk Factors in Orthopedic Surgeries
author: Santos, Gabriel, et al.

steps.title: Place surface electrodes
steps.instruction: Place two surface electrodes on the belly of each target muscle (biceps femoris, rectus femoris, gastrocnemius lateralis) on both lower limbs, spaced 2 cm apart and aligned with the muscle fibers according to SENIAM guidelines; locate biceps femoris at the midpoint between the ischial tuberosity and the lateral epicondyle of the tibia, rectus femoris at the midpoint between the anterosuperior iliac spine and the patella, gastrocnemius lateralis one‑third of the distance between the head of the fibula and the heel; place a reference electrode at the external malleolus.

substeps.instruction: Locate biceps femoris midpoint (ischial tuberosity ↔ lateral epicondyle of tibia) and attach two electrodes 2 cm apart.
Locate rectus femoris midpoint (anterosuperior iliac spine ↔ patella) and attach two electrodes 2 cm apart.
Locate gastrocnemius lateralis (one‑third distance head of fibula ↔ heel) and attach two electrodes 2 cm apart.
Place reference electrode on the external malleolus.

steps.title: Determine biceps femoris MVC
steps.instruction: Position the participant prone with the knee flexed to approximately 45° and the leg externally rotated; the researcher applies pressure to the ankle region to counteract knee flexion; have the participant perform a maximal voluntary contraction (MVC) of the biceps femoris and record the baseline EMG.

steps.title: Determine rectus femoris MVC
steps.instruction: Seat the participant with thighs fully supported on the table; the participant uses the upper limbs for trunk stability by gripping the table edge or placing hands on either side; instruct the participant to perform hip flexion with neutral rotation while the researcher provides resistance; record the MVC EMG for the rectus femoris.

steps.title: Determine gastrocnemius MVC
steps.instruction: Ask the participant to stand with weight on the limb to be tested (optional finger support on a table); instruct the participant to perform maximal plantar flexion of the tested limb; repeat the contraction three times and record the baseline EMG for the gastrocnemius lateralis.

steps.title: Place IMU motion sensors
steps.instruction: Attach seven wireless T‑SENS IMU sensors following the manufacturer’s guidelines: for each lower limb, place a thigh sensor on the upper leg above the knee facing forward, a shank sensor on the lower leg above the ankle facing outward, and a foot sensor on top of the foot (or in the shoelaces); place one sensor on the sacrum, centered on the participant’s back, to record hip posture; ensure all sensors are secured with the supplied adjustable straps.

steps.title: Calibrate IMU sensors
steps.instruction: In a magnetically neutral environment (free of metal or magnets), initialize the IMU system and perform calibration by having the participant hold two standing postures, each for 6 seconds: (1) arms alongside the body, torso and head neutral, feet parallel hip‑width apart; (2) arms extended perpendicular to the torso, palms perpendicular to the ground, legs bent; confirm a positive calibration test before proceeding.

steps.title: Begin synchronized data recording
steps.instruction: After IMU calibration (performed before the surgical scrubbing process), start simultaneous EMG recording (OpenSignals) and kinematic recording (CAPTIV) when the surgeon positions the patient for surgery; insert a CAPTIV trigger to mark the onset and conclusion of each task; also log the surgery type and the patient’s body posture on the operating table.

steps.title: Pre‑test validation tasks
steps.instruction: In a laboratory setting, have participants perform seven standing tasks with 1 minute rest between tasks: 1) hold 2 kg with both hands and slight trunk flexion (≤20°) for 5 minutes; 2) simulate sewing on a table for 5 minutes; 3) simulate hammering while rotating trunk, left foot forward, right foot plantar‑flexed, right knee flexed to 35°, hip extended 15°, repeat 15 times; 4) simulate hammering with body close to table, feet parallel and anterior, repeat 15 times; 5) trunk flexion over table with hands supported, shoulders flexed, arms extended, left foot plantar‑flexed, maintain for 5 minutes; 6) same as 5) but with both feet plantar‑flexed for 5 minutes; 7) lateral displacement of a box between perpendicular tables: carry box close to body with elbows at 90°, move laterally, rotate trunk and squat to place box on left‑side table, repeat 15 times. Record EMG and IMU data for each task.

steps.title: Preprocess kinematic and EMG data
steps.instruction: In CAPTIV, convert rotation quaternions to joint angles (degrees); export EMG CSV files from OpenSignals, import them into CAPTIV, and synchronize the EMG with the kinematic data.

steps.title: Compute RMS and normalize EMG
steps.instruction: Within CAPTIV, calculate the root‑mean‑square (RMS) envelope of each muscle’s EMG using a 100‑sample window, average the signal, and normalize each RMS value by the maximum value obtained during its respective MVC to express activity as %MVC.

steps.title: Export outcomes and visualize
steps.instruction: Export %MVC values for biceps femoris, rectus femoris, and gastrocnemius lateralis together with joint‑angle time series (hip flexion/extension, hip internal/external rotation, hip abduction/adduction, knee flexion, knee internal/external rotation, ankle dorsiflexion/plantar‑flexion, ankle inversion/eversion) as CSV files; optionally view the 3‑D avatar of the kinematic data in CAPTIV.
